# Tensile test analysis

Elastic modulus was estimated as the slope of an ordinary least-squares linear fit, stress = intercept + E × strain, using all recorded points for each material. The fits therefore include the full measured strain range; no separate elastic-window selection was supplied.

![Stress–strain data and linear fits](stress_strain_fits.svg)

| Material | Measurements | Specimens | Strain range | Modulus (GPa) | Intercept (MPa) | R² |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| aluminum | 30 | 3 | 0.0002–0.0020 | 69.38 | -0.31 | 0.99834 |
| steel | 30 | 3 | 0.0002–0.0020 | 199.06 | 0.62 | 0.99844 |
| titanium | 30 | 3 | 0.0002–0.0020 | 116.56 | -0.77 | 0.99788 |

Modulus values are the fitted slopes converted from MPa to GPa. The intercepts are included because the unconstrained fits were not forced through the origin. R² summarizes how closely each full-range data set follows a straight line; a high value does not establish that every point lies in the elastic regime. For material properties requiring a strict elastic modulus, refit only the initial linear elastic portion identified from the test protocol or stress–strain curves.

item.text:
Created the [results write-up](</private/tmp/tmpgu45y52d/pete/projects/elastic-modulus/results.md>) and [stress–strain figure](</private/tmp/tmpgu45y52d/pete/projects/elastic-modulus/stress_strain_fits.svg>).

Using ordinary least-squares fits across each material’s full measured strain range, the estimated moduli are **69.38 GPa for aluminum**, **199.06 GPa for steel**, and **116.56 GPa for titanium**. Each fit uses 30 measurements from 3 specimens. The write-up includes the fit intercepts and R² values, and notes that a strict elastic modulus estimate may require fitting only the initial linear elastic region.
